problems.title: Vertical-flip flag binds to the flow argument
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF p.6; stereosr_image_dataset.py, lines 65–70; BasicSR 1.3.5 transforms.py, augment
claim: The caller expects four augmented images and passes its vertical-flip Boolean as the fourth positional argument.
analysis: The pinned signature is augment(imgs, hflip, rotation, flows, return_status). The flags bind flows to True. With rotation disabled and a sampled false horizontal flip, the dependency returns the pair consisting of the four-image list and that flow value. The caller unpacks two outer values into four variables and must fail. Valid scale-four image pairs of spatial sizes \(256\times256\) and \(64\times64\) do not alter this contract. Other random branches may fail earlier while manipulating the Boolean as flow.
result: The released caller/dependency combination has a sufficient loader failure. It does not establish that no privately patched training environment existed.
repair: Use a shared explicit horizontal/vertical image transformation returning four images. Moving the vertical flag into the dependency’s rotation argument would also enable transpose behavior and is not equivalent.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: Standalone export selects the left channels twice
claim: Both standalone output branches spatially crop the same six-channel tensor and select the same first three channels.
analysis: For stereo RGB levels \((0.1,0.2,0.3)\) and \((0.7,0.8,0.9)\), both branches export BGR \((0.3,0.2,0.1)\), whereas the right branch should export \((0.9,0.8,0.7)\). The indexing discards channels \(3\)–\(5\). The script also references a local image variable before assignment, so this is a latent defect after that earlier blocker. The separate model-validation path correctly splits at channel \(3\).
result: This export path loses the right view when views differ. The correct validation path prevents inferring that published stereo averages necessarily used duplicate left images.
repair: Split the six-channel output into channels \(0\)–\(2\) and \(3\)–\(5\) before spatial cropping and color conversion.

problems.title: The release does not identify the narrated training protocol
problems.source_location: Sections 4.1 and 4.3.1, PDF pp.6,9; training YAML lines 78–83; diffssr_arch.py, line 256
claim: The paper describes \(500{,}000\) iterations with cosine decay and selects window \(3\); the release uses \(800{,}000\) iterations, MultiStepLR and window \(5\).
analysis: The first released milestone is \(600{,}000\), so it has not fired by the paper’s endpoint \(500{,}000\), where the stated cosine decay would be complete. The main stereo scores agree with the window-\(5\) ablation row, which supports an alternative run interpretation but does not identify every checkpoint. The paper also studies test-time window changes. Per-GPU batch size and global batch size are not silently equated.
result: The artifact mismatch is established, but the exact historical experiment recipe remains unresolved.
repair: Associate each checkpoint/table row with its actual configuration, dependencies, seed, duration and training/test window. Do not replace these with a guessed recipe.
